name: Kell's Tally
summary: Forty-one years of silence-bell records from Ashveil Cross: every silent-ring, date, duration, and weather, kept in sealed tubes by Warden Kell and her predecessor. It is the continent's only long-series measurement of the Quiet's behavior — better data than anything the Veil-Wardens or Censer possess, which is exactly why both want it and why Kell has released neither.
origin: ~771 AA onward; maintained continuously through two wardenships
current_whereabouts: The tally-house at Ashveil Cross — a reinforced room with its own well, because Kell does not trust either of her paymasters' archives.
properties: Shows the Quiet's advance is not steady: it moves in bursts that correlate with nothing visible
Records three 'all-bells' events before this year's — each followed within a season by a Glimmerborn birth nearby
Written in Kell's personal shorthand; only she and her late predecessor read it fluently
keepers: Warden Otta Kell. The Veil-Wardens would trade much for copies; the Censer forbids their release; the Reeve's court pretends not to know they exist.
value_or_danger: The data itself is harmless. Whoever controls it controls what the continent knows about the Quiet — and when.
adventure_hooks: Kell offers players sealed duplicates for escort to the Veil-Wardens — without either paymaster learning.
A tube is found opened and resealed, one year's records subtly altered. Only two people could have; one is dead.
Kell's shorthand proves to be Old Weaver notation adapted for numbers — she has been writing forbidden language for forty-one years without knowing.

rarity.note: Paper, ink, and forty-one years of discipline.
